tasks.short: Open the case file from court and prison data, file documents and letters, write contact notes, keep report deadlines, and check the case folder before handover or closing.

steps.what: Probation officer prepares the case folder from court and prison papers
Probation officer files documents, reports and letters in the case folder
Probation officer writes contact notes after each meeting with the offender

loop.input: The officer's spoken summary straight after the meeting.
loop.output: A draft contact note in the case system's fields.
loop.check: A validator flags every statement on risk, violence or substance use and every name not in the case. The officer reads every note against the summary and the meeting, checks that it says what happened and nothing more, corrects it and approves it; unclear notes are typed.
loop.stop: One draft per contact; if the officer rejects it, they write the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Plain dictation gives a transcript, not a note in the case fields.

steps.what: Probation officer keeps report deadlines in a spreadsheet
Probation officer checks the case folder before handover or closing

tasks.design: Court orders and prison data arrive through the justice chain exchange and prefill the case in the case system ({OTHER}). Incoming documents by e-mail are filed to the case by case number. After a meeting the officer speaks a short summary and a bounded step drafts the contact note; a validator flags every risk statement, and the officer corrects and approves each note. Report deadlines follow from the court order as timers. No software scores re-offending risk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Papers were retyped, documents filed by hand and deadlines kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Justice chain exchanges carry case data; speech tools draft notes into case systems.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can contain invented statements, and risk statements carry weight in court.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a note that is fair to the offender and clear for the next officer.
tasks.altitude: The officer checks drafted notes and prefilled files instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether case folders are complete at handover.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or letter in the care record.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation in AI-drafted notes.
Inspectie JenV found the Reclassering's OxRec formulas swapped since 2018, putting about 21% of cases in another risk category; use was paused in February 2026.
AI that assesses re-offending risk is high-risk under Annex III 6(d); here no software scores risk.

assumptions: Boundary: from the court order to the folder checked; advice reports to court are outside.
Input contract: chain data from courts and prisons; fallback is retyping papers.

The officer approves every note; drafts never go to court unread. s3 keeps 75 because every note is read and corrected and summaries miss nuance. s1 keeps 40 for papers that do not come through the chain.
A DPIA and works council consent come before use.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a risk statement the officer did not say?

already_counted.description: Probation officer reads and corrects drafted notes.

incremental.description: Probation officer checks prefilled chain data against the court order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: chain data are often incomplete and drafts are mostly rewritten, so s1 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 90 (33.5); high: chain data and drafts as designed (44.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with the offender, talk with families, friends and others with relevant information, request records from police, prison and care providers, and write background notes.

steps.what: Probation officer gathers information about offenders' backgrounds by talking to the offender
Probation officer talks to families, friends and other people with relevant information
Probation officer receives police and prison records through the chain exchange and prepares requests for care records
Probation officer explains the consent form and the offender signs it for the care records
Probation officer checks each care-record request: records asked, the signed consent and the care provider
Probation officer sends the checked requests to the care providers and receives the records
Probation officer writes the background notes

tasks.design: Records from police and prison come through the justice chain exchange into the case system ({OTHER}); care providers send records on a request form with the offender's consent. Background notes go into structured fields (family, work, housing, substance use, earlier offences). Talking with the offender and others stays with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were requested by e-mail and phone, and notes were free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Chain exchanges and consent-based record requests exist in the Dutch justice chain.
tasks.still_hard: Families may not want to talk or may not tell the whole story.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a mother does not say about her son.

reach.learn: Whether advice reports rest on complete records.

evidence.claim: Case systems can receive records through chain exchanges and hold structured background fields.
Health data such as addiction treatment are special category data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the case folder to background notes; the advice report is outside.
Input contract: chain data from police and prisons; care records only with consent; fallback is e-mail and phone.
Talking with the offender and others, consent and the check before requests go out do not change. s4 keeps 85 because the officer writes the notes; only copying earlier offences and chain data goes.
research_questions: Do records arrive before the first talk more often?

incremental.description: No new work: explaining the consent form is shown as step s3a.

approvals.approved_version: Each care-record request with the records asked for and the offender's signed consent exactly as checked by the officer in s3b, sent once to the named care provider; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: care providers do not use the request form and chain data are often late, so s3 keeps 80 (4.6); high: chain exchange and request form as designed (8.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule appointments with probationers, interview them regularly about progress and conditions, check test and treatment results, and record the interview and assessment.

steps.what: Probation officer sets appointments with probationers in the case system; by phone and letter today
Probation officer checks the appointment before it goes: date, place, the probationer and their phone number
Probation officer sends the checked appointment with its text reminders to the probationer
Probation officer interviews probationers and parolees to evaluate their progress in accomplishing goals
Probation officer checks drug test results and treatment attendance against the probation terms
Probation officer records the interview and assessment of progress

tasks.design: Appointments are set in the case system ({OTHER}) and probationers get text reminders, so fewer calls and letters are needed. Drug test results and treatment attendance from providers show per probationer against the probation terms. The interview record uses fields per goal and condition. Interviewing and judging progress stay with the officer; no software decides on violations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointments were set by phone and letter and results came by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems send reminders and receive provider results.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a slip from a relapse.

evidence.claim: Case systems can send text reminders and show provider results per client.
No adverse decision may rest solely on automated processing under GDPR article 22.

assumptions: Boundary: from the supervision plan to the progress record; reporting violations to the prosecutor is outside.
Input contract: results from labs and treatment providers; fallback is e-mail.
Probationers read text reminders; no added probationer time.
Interviewing and the check of each appointment do not change. s4 keeps 85 because the officer writes the assessment; only copying test results and attendance goes.

incremental.description: Probation officer updates probationers' phone numbers.

approvals.approved_version: The appointment with date and place exactly as checked by the officer in s1b, sent once with its text reminders to that probationer's phone; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many labs and providers keep sending results by e-mail, so s3 keeps 80 (10.3); high: results shown per probationer as designed (14.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the conversation from the case file, discuss with the offender how drug and alcohol abuse or anger problems played roles in the offence, and note the conversation.

steps.what: Probation officer prepares the conversation from the case file
Probation officer discusses with offenders how drug and alcohol abuse and anger management problems played roles in their criminal behavior
Probation officer notes the conversation

tasks.design: The case system ({OTHER}) shows the offender's history, earlier talks and treatment on one screen for preparation, and the officer writes the conversation note as today; it is a first record and keeps its time. The conversation itself stays with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier notes had to be read one by one and notes were free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems show case summaries and structured note fields.
tasks.still_hard: Offenders often deny a link between substance use and the offence.
tasks.human_edge: Helping an offender see the pattern without shaming them.

evidence.claim: Case systems can show case summaries and structured note fields.
Notes on substance use are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the case folder to the conversation noted; treatment is outside.
Input contract: case history in the case system; fallback is reading notes one by one.
research_questions: Are notes on substance use more complete?

incremental.description: No new work: the one-screen view needs no upkeep by the officer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much history sits outside the case system, so s1 keeps 85 (1.5); high: one screen as designed (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The probation officer keeps talking with offenders and families, judging progress and writing what matters; retyped papers, filed e-mails and free-text notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes for invented statements
role.ambitious_version: An officer with more time for each offender.

job.title: Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists
